title: Private VPC Capacity Corridor Calculator
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, practical capacity calculator and BOM estimator for Private/VPC deployments that focuses on a two-band "capacity corridor": baseline (steady-state) and surge (short-lived demand corridors). The intent is to produce quick SKU-level BOMs and utilization/latency tradeoffs for customer sizing conversations and procurement pre-approvals.

How to use (high level):
1) Fill workload profile inputs in the Inputs section. Most of the downstream numbers are derived.
2) Choose tiling strategy (per-request tiling or multi-model packing) and quantization profile.
3) Run the corridor projection to see baseline vs. surge lane counts, spare inventory, and CAPEX.
4) Use the region split knobs to generate per-region BOMs for purchase orders.

Assumptions and terminology:
- Baseline QPS: sustained queries per second over 5m window.
- Surge corridor: short bursts window (typically 1–10 minutes) where latency SLOs must be met.
- Effective tokens per request: average generated + prompt tokens used to pick memory/KV cache sizing.
- KV cache hit ratio: fraction of tokens served from prefix/KV cache (reduces GPU work).
- Tile size: number of concurrent sequences a single GPU can hold for prompt+generation.
- Safe spare ratio: percentage of extra nodes to keep on-hand for replacement and immediate burst capacity.

Inputs (example values in parentheses):
- Baseline QPS: (120)
- Surge factor: (3.5) => Surge QPS = Baseline * Surge factor = 420
- Avg tokens per request: (80)
- Avg latency budget (ms): (150)
- Model variant: (redwood-llm-13b-int8)
- Effective throughput per GPU (tokens/s): (12,000) -- derived from kernel selection/seq len profile
- Tile occupancy per GPU: (64 concurrent sequences)
- KV cache hit ratio: (0.25)
- Target utilization (baseline): (0.65)
- Target utilization (surge lane): (0.90)
- Spare ratio: (0.10)
- On-prem procurement lead time (weeks): (8)
- Replacement MTTR target (hours): (4)

Derivations and quick formulas (for sheet cells):
- Baseline token demand (tokens/s) = Baseline QPS * Avg tokens per request
- Surge token demand (tokens/s) = Baseline token demand * Surge factor
- Effective token work after KV cache = tokens/s * (1 - KV cache hit ratio)
- GPU capacity (tokens/s) = Effective throughput per GPU (adjusted for quantization/seq length)
- GPUs needed (baseline, raw) = ceil( Baseline effective tokens/s / (GPU capacity * target utilization) )
- GPUs needed (surge lane) = ceil( Surge effective tokens/s / (GPU capacity * target utilization for surge) )
- Total active GPUs = max(baseline raw, surge lane) if we plan to absorb surge via autoscaling within the corridor; otherwise show two-lane layout with separate baseline + surge reserve.
- Spare units = ceil(total active GPUs * spare ratio)

Sample compute run (numbers from inputs above):
- Baseline token demand = 120 QPS * 80 tokens = 9,600 tokens/s
- After KV cache (25% hit) => 9,600 * 0.75 = 7,200 tokens/s
- GPU capacity per node = 12,000 tokens/s
- Baseline GPUs raw = ceil(7,200 / (12,000 * 0.65)) = ceil(7,200 / 7,800) = 1
- Surge token demand = 9,600 * 3.5 = 33,600 tokens/s => after cache = 25,200 tokens/s
- Surge GPUs raw = ceil(25,200 / (12,000 * 0.90)) = ceil(25,200 / 10,800) = 3
- Corridor layout recommendation: baseline lane = 1 GPU, surge lane = 2 additional GPUs pre-warmed (total active 3), spare 10% = 1 spare => Purchase = 4 GPUs

BOM estimator (example SKU table rows as CSV lines to paste into procurement sheet):
SKU,Description,Unit GPU Equivalent (vGPU),Qty,Unit price (USD),Extended cost (USD)

NVLink-Cable-75cm,Inter-node NVLink cabling (per pair),0,2,350,700
Rack-1U-1200W,Rack power distribution per node,0,4,650,2600
Support-3yr-Onsite,3-year onsite HW support (per node),0,4,1600,6400
Total, , , , ,57700

Cost sensitivity knobs to test (suggested sheet scenarios):
- Swap quantization profile to int4 => GPU capacity increases ~1.6x, which reduces GPU count and unit economics; update kernel/latency trade-off cell.
- Increase KV cache ratio via prefix caching integration => reduces tokens/s proportionally.
- Change tiling: larger tile occupancy trades off peak latency fairness vs throughput; include a cell that shows percentile tail cost impact.

Regional split and lead time planning:
- Use region fraction knobs (US-West 60%, EU 30%, APAC 10%) to split the Purchase BOM by region.
- Add procurement lead-time multiplier to ensure additional spare units to cover MTTR and lead time: Spare_for_lead_time = ceil((lead_time_weeks / (MTTR_hours / 168)) * mean_replacement_rate). For quick planning default add +1 node per 8-week lead time per 10 nodes.

Operational guidance and meeting notes (short):
- For first customer PO, recommend conservative spare + 2 GPUs for burst lanes if latency SLOs are strict and cannot rely on cross-region fallback.
- Validate model kernel profile with Performance team: run a 30-minute mixed QPS trace to verify tokens/s per GPU under chosen quantization.
- Add an A/B pilot: ship baseline lane only, observe 72h steady-state, then request surge lane allocation if observed baseline tail approaches utilization >70%.

Open questions for procurement/legal before finalizing PO:
- Acceptable on-site support SLA tier? (next business day vs. 4hr)
- Warranty and transfer-of-ownership clause for repurposed hardware.
- Import duties for APAC region and recommended local reseller.

Appendix (quick copy-paste formulas for spreadsheet cells):
- cell B10 = B2 * B3   # baseline tokens/s = QPS * avg tokens
- cell B12 = B10 * (1 - B6)  # after cache
- cell B14 = CEILING(B12 / (B8 * B9), 1)  # GPUs needed

Notes/history:
- Drafted after 2025 Q4 capacity review, requested by solutions-eng for three upcoming private deals with tight latency SLOs.
- Next revision: add power/cooling delta per region and rack provisioning worksheet for datacenter floor planning.
